items.title: Workflow is 10x faster, again
items.summary: 5.8 runs workflows on a new execution engine, rebuilt for performance. Step-to-step latency is 12x lower, and large fan-outs, like running 256 steps in parallel, use 14x less function time outside your step code. This directly improves turn times for , among many other improvements.Workflow SDKdurable AI agentsTo get the new engine, upgrade to  or later. New runs will use the new engine by default, and runs already started on an older version will safely keep running on that version. Make sure your steps are  to get the most out of this upgrade.workflow@5.8.0idempotent where possibleIn our  comparing  to , p75 step-to-step overhead fell from 85 ms to 7 ms. The median run, including 102 seconds of step work, finished in 111 seconds instead of 3.0 minutes. Running 256 parallel steps in a fan-out added 5.5× less overhead, 2.5 seconds instead of 13.5 seconds, and the median run spent 14× less time in functions beyond the steps' own work, 105 seconds instead of 1,446. A five-turn agent loop that streams its tokens through durable streams and calls tools added 0.9 seconds of overhead instead of 3.0 seconds, 3.3× less. Consult the  for how we measure these numbers.benchmarksbenchmarks page5.2.05.8.0Resuming after 1 second idle time went from 425 ms to 184 ms, 2.3× faster. Resumptions more than 5 seconds out might see slightly larger overhead. You can choose to  to optimize time-to-resume at the cost of additional compute time.keep functions warm for longerMany of the above benefits rely on speculative execution of Steps. Only Steps that are idempotent can be run in this way. A step that passes its  as an , like the Stripe charge below, is already safe and needs no changes.
